body:
[A10] Opened so the residue named on docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md has a tracker of its own, raised by the review of PR #431 (issue #406).

## What is pinned today and what is not

PR #431 pins the STEP SEQUENCE of the seven jobs of the RTL workflow: their recognised steps, in order, refused when one is inserted, removed or reordered. Where no specialized script pin applies, it does not pin the CONTENT: a recognised command may change while the sequence stays intact. The sibling full-ci-gate SHA-pin step also lacks a content pin, as measured and added to this scope by the decision below.

The four non-RTL carriers have the matching work scoped on #407, which is titled for those carriers and covers only them. The RTL half was previously said to ride #295's widened acceptance row; #295 is closed, so the RTL half currently has no tracker. That is the gap this issue fills.

Additional settled scope: [full-ci-gate SHA-pin decision](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/439#issuecomment-5772547851).

## Objective

A recognised step of an RTL job, and the sibling full-ci-gate SHA-pin step, cannot change what it runs without the pin refusing, in the same shape the four carriers get on #407.

## Acceptance

1. Every recognised step of the seven RTL jobs, plus full-ci-gate's "Print the event and pin the one SHA this run validates" run step, carries a content pin, in whatever form the carriers' pin takes when #407 lands, so the two halves read the same way.
2. A changed command in a recognised step is refused by name, and the refusal names the job and the step.
3. The pin cannot pass vacuously: an empty content record and a step whose recorded content no longer exists are each refused, each with an arm.
4. The pristine tree stays green and the arm count does not fall.
5. The SHA-pin controls reject deleting the checkout-HEAD mismatch assertion, replacing its exit 1 with true, and swallowing each normalized line. Matching legitimate script/record maintenance stays possible. The policy accurately describes both the seven-job and sibling-step coverage.

## Authority and scope

docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md items 4 and 12; the step-sequence table PR #431 adds to scripts/ci_events.py; #407 for the carrier half. Out of scope: the step sequence itself, which #406 closes, and the membership authority of the table, which #406's review also raised and its lane answers.

Lane and review: A181 completed source `f01f237d4b48c7b1ed59c80aca51430901791624`; the 48 static/builder checks pass and native validation is running. Internal R254 Codex and external R255 Opus are reserved. [The source-lane decision](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/439#issuecomment-5782501927) permits parallel source work; final composition follows #504 and requires current-dev validation and fresh applicable review. This remains outside the October critical path.

[A10] SCOPE DECISION BEFORE TAKEOVER - include the sibling SHA-pin step

[PR505 R220-2 F3](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/505#issuecomment-5772521129) measured one additional unpinned script outside the seven RTL jobs: full-ci-gate step 2, "Print the event and pin the one SHA this run validates". Deleting its checkout-HEAD mismatch assertion or replacing exit 1 with true leaves ci_events --check green. The other 11 sibling run steps reject the measured replacement/swallowing controls. [Independent p7/p11 receipts](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/tree/841d969d65a52b9ac0ec5c6012c32cd5ff3abd67/review-evidence/505-r1/round2/reviews/R220-2).

This issue is Ready and has no executor, implementation branch or frozen active lane. Expand its future scope to cover that single SHA-pin step alongside the seven RTL jobs already listed. Use the same canonical normalized-script policy as #407, with named first-differing-line refusals, matching maintenance updates and nonvacuous controls. At minimum, the SHA-pin controls must reject deleting the mismatch assertion, replacing exit 1 with true, and swallowing each normalized line; a matching legitimate record/script edit must remain possible. Existing specialized pins and step/membership authority remain unchanged.

This records the pre-existing executable gap; PR505's F3 is the separate inaccurate residue sentence and must be corrected there. No acceptance criterion of the active #407 lane changes. Do not claim this gap closed until #439 implements and validates the pin. The older "machine-checked" policy wording must then describe the actual scope accurately.

These share files, so do not edit or borrow the active #504 lane. Use a separate issue branch from dev, preserve all carrier records and specialize only the accepted RTL content scope. After #504 lands, any shared-artifact composition must receive full current-dev candidate validation and fresh applicable review coverage. No speculative final candidate, hidden contract union or early merge is authorized.

Validation: pristine ci_events --check/--selftest, per-step content changes refused with job/step/first differing normalized line, missing/empty/stale canonical records, every normalized-line swallowing control, the named SHA mismatch assertion deletions/true replacement, matching legitimate record-and-script maintenance, and all existing populations preserved. Use the default self-test owner, relevant docs/idiom/evidence/fail-fast checks and exact source integrity. Manager owns full local/native, trusted act, mandatory hosted, independent reviews and final merge/post-merge bar. No workflow schedule, membership authority, normalization semantics, processor pin, product behavior or hardware change is in scope.
